articleTitle: Microwave ferrites
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper is a tutorial review of microwave ferrites for electrical engineers. It is in three sections. The first examines the chemical and crystal compositions and their effects on the microwave properties of ferrite. The second part discusses the magnetic and microwave properties and explains how non-reciprocity arises in ferrites. In the third part the imposition of non-reciprocal characteristics on the four-wave phenomena by the inclusion of magnetized ferrite Is shown to lead to the following four waveguide effects: Faraday rotation, field displacement, non-reciprocal phase shift and gyromagnetic resonance. Each of these Is discussed and an examination of at least one practical application of each is made, as well as their limitations of operation In frequency and power. The isolator is studied in detail, as the various methods of isolation form the basis for several other applications. The generation of these from one or other of the isolators is discussed. Finally, the paper shows how a non-reciprocal waveguide effect can be made reciprocal by a suitable adjustment of the configuration.

articleTitle: The measurement of rainfall over large areas using radar
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper reviews the theoretical and experimental aspects of the quantitative measurement of rainfall by radar. During World War II the theoretical foundations of the use of radar in the field of rainfall measurement were laid. Subsequent experimental work proved that the precision attainable when measuring rainfall rate was disappointing. Some recent theoretical work has led to complete agreement between theory and experiment. The use of radar in the quantitative measurement of rainfall is limited only by the relationship between raindrop size distribution and rainfall rate.

articleTitle: Silicon avalanche rectifier diodes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: These diodes have reverse power dissipation rating equal to their forward rating and represent a new concept in the design of silicon diodes. They have avalanche properties in the reverse direction similar to those of a Zener diode. This type of diffused junction silicon rectifier is especially processed to ensure that the reverse voltage breakdown occurs in the bulk material of the junction and not at one small point on the surface. This arrangement gives the rectifiers the ability to absorb reverse over-voltage transients, and leads to an improved long-term stability in the reverse characteristics. For conventional devices, the peak inverse voltage is one of the characteristics which is susceptible to change, often with disastrous results on the equipment in which it is installed.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Investigations of electric breakdown in dust-laden atmospheres are described.
